Yes, the story has an appropriate balance between scene and summary/exposition. 

The writer effectively alternates between the two elements to maintain a steady, engaging pace across the span of nearly a year. Summary and exposition are used early on to quickly establish the backstory (how Nora and Daniel met, their wedding, and Miss Emily's business history) and later to bridge the gaps in time (moving from autumn to spring to June). Meanwhile, the emotional core and character development of the story unfold in real-time scenes featuring vivid dialogue and subtle interactions—such as the restaurant lunch, the hospital benefit, the birthday party kitchen conversation, and the final encounter at the supermarket register.
